questions.text: Suppose U is the power set of the set S={1,2,3,4,5,6}. For any T[latex]\in[/latex]U, let |T| denote the number of elements in T and T' denote the complement of T. For any T,R[latex]\in[/latex]U, let T\R be the set of all elements in T which are not in R. Which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
[latex]X\setminus Y=X\cap Y'[/latex] and [latex]Y'\setminus X'=Y'\cap X[/latex]. These are the same set for every X, Y.

- Option 1 fails for X = {1}.
- Option 2: two 5-element subsets of a 6-element set must overlap.
- Option 3 is not true for all X, Y.

Answer: [latex]\forall X\,\forall Y\,(X\setminus Y=Y'\setminus X')[/latex]

options: [latex]\exists X\in U \; \exists Y\in U \; [/latex] [latex](|X|=5,\; |Y|=5 \; and \;  X \cap  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X\in U \; \forall Y\in U \;[/latex] [latex] (|X|=2,\; |Y|=3 \; and \; X \setminus  Y=\phi )[/latex]
[latex]\forall X \in U \; \forall Y\in U\; (X \setminus  Y=Y' \setminus  X')[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the relation X(P,Q,R,S,T,U) with the following set of functional dependencies
F= {{P,R}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{S,T}, {P,S,U}[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]{Q,R} }
Which of the following is the trivial functional dependency in [latex]F^{+}[/latex], where [latex]F^{+}[/latex] is closure of F ?
questions.solution:
A dependency is trivial when its right side is a subset of its left side.

{S} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] {P, S}, so {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S} is trivial. In option 2, T is not in {P, R}.

Answer: {P, S} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {S}

questions.text: Among simple LR (SLR) , canonical LR, and look-ahead LR (LALR), which of the following pairs identify the method that is very easy to implement and the method that is the most powerful , in that order?
questions.solution:
SLR uses LR(0) items with FOLLOW sets, so it is the simplest. Canonical LR(1) has the most states and recognises the largest class of grammars (most powerful). LALR lies in between.

Answer: SLR, canonical LR
